## 1. TEgenomeSimulator vs denovoTEeval

```{r, load_files_tegs, echo=FALSE}
# item28/29: 5 duplicate runs (item29_sim_mode0_raw.sh); reps 1:5 reused for Comparison 2 below
reps <- 1:5

tegs_c1_list <- lapply(reps, function(i){
  gfai <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/mode0/TEgenomeSimulator_m0_chr10000k_rep%d_result/m0_chr10000k_rep%d_genome_sequence_out_final.fasta.fai', i, i))
  tfai <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/mode0/TEgenomeSimulator_m0_chr10000k_rep%d_result/m0_chr10000k_rep%d_repeat_sequence_out_final.fasta.fai', i, i))
  gff  <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/mode0/TEgenomeSimulator_m0_chr10000k_rep%d_result/m0_chr10000k_rep%d_repeat_annotation_out_final.gff', i, i))
  list(
    genomefai = read.table(gfai, header = F, sep = '\t'),
    tefai = read.table(tfai, header = F, sep = '\t', comment.char = ""),
    tegff = read.table(gff, header = F, sep = '\t', comment.char = "")
  )
})

# rep 1 aliased to the original single-genome variable names, used unchanged by the
# composition piechart sections (1.02-1.04) further down
genomefai1 <- tegs_c1_list[[1]]$genomefai
tefai1 <- tegs_c1_list[[1]]$tefai
tegff1 <- tegs_c1_list[[1]]$tegff
```

```{r, data_sum_tegs, include=FALSE}
breakdown1 <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegff1)
data.sum1 <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(tegff1)

breakdown1_allreps <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){
  bd <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegs_c1_list[[i]]$tegff)
  bd$rep <- i
  bd
}))
```

```{r, load_files_denovote, echo=FALSE}
# item28/29: 5 duplicate runs (item29_denovoTEeval_raw.sh); rep i imports rep i's TEGS
# composition table, so rep i is a paired comparison against tegs_c1_list[[i]]
dnvte_c1_list <- lapply(reps, function(i){
  gfai <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/denovoTEeval/denovoTEeval_rep%d/m0_chr10000k_rep%d_out_sequence_nest.fasta.fai', i, i))
  tfai <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/denovoTEeval/denovoTEeval_rep%d/m0_chr10000k_rep%d_out_repeats.fasta.fai', i, i))
  gff  <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/denovoTEeval/denovoTEeval_rep%d/m0_chr10000k_rep%d_out_repeats_nest.gff', i, i))
  list(
    genomefai = read.table(gfai, header = F, sep = '\t'),
    tefai = read.table(tfai, header = F, sep = '\t', comment.char = ""),
    tegff = convert_denovote_gff(read.table(gff, header = F, sep = '\t', comment.char = ""))
  )
})

genomefai2 <- dnvte_c1_list[[1]]$genomefai
tefai2 <- dnvte_c1_list[[1]]$tefai
tegff2 <- dnvte_c1_list[[1]]$tegff
```

```{r, data_sum_denovote, include=FALSE}
breakdown2 <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(tegff2)
data.sum2 <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(tegff2)

breakdown2_allreps <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){
  bd <- te_breakdown_sim_genome(dnvte_c1_list[[i]]$tegff)
  bd$rep <- i
  bd
}))
```

### 1.01 The proportion of TE/nonTE sequence (mean ± SD, n = 5 replicates)
**Important:** denovoTE-eval doesn't update simulated repeat.fa after nested insertion. So the TE bases calculated from its output repeat.fa doesn't include nested TE insertion sequences. Need to calculate TE bases from TE gff file.

```{r, get_stat, echo=FALSE}
tegs_c1_stat <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){
  gsize <- sum(tegs_c1_list[[i]]$genomefai$V2)
  tesize <- sum(tegs_c1_list[[i]]$tefai$V2)
  data.frame(rep = i, simulator = "TEGS", genomesize = gsize, tesize = tesize)
}))

dnvte_c1_stat <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(reps, function(i){
  gsize <- sum(dnvte_c1_list[[i]]$genomefai$V2)
  tesize <- dnvte_c1_list[[i]]$tegff |> mutate(V10 = V5 - V4 + 1) |> pull(V10) |> sum()
  data.frame(rep = i, simulator = "dnvTEe", genomesize = gsize, tesize = tesize)
}))

stat_c <- dplyr::bind_rows(tegs_c1_stat, dnvte_c1_stat) |>
  mutate(nonte = genomesize - tesize) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(tesize, nonte), names_to = "feature", values_to = "bases") |>
  mutate(feature = dplyr::recode(feature, tesize = "TE", nonte = "nonTE")) |>
  mutate(perc = 100 * bases / genomesize)

df_stat <- stat_c |>
  group_by(simulator, feature) |>
  summarise(mean_bases = mean(bases), sd_bases = sd(bases),
            mean_perc = mean(perc), sd_perc = sd(perc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(simulator = factor(simulator, levels = c("dnvTEe", "TEGS")),
         feature = factor(feature, levels = c("TE", "nonTE")))
```

```{r, plot_stat_tegs_denovote, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 3.4, fig.asp = 0.75}
plotwidth <- 3.4
plotheight <- 2.55
plot <- plot_te_nonte_bars_meansd(df_stat, "TE/nonTE-occupied bases \ndnvTEe vs TEGS (mean ± SD, n=5)")
options(repr.plot.width=plotwidth, repr.plot.height=plotheight)
plot
```


```{r, save_fig1.01.01, echo=FALSE}
png(filename = paste0(OUT, "nonTEbases_dnvTEvTEGS.png"), width = plotwidth, height = plotheight, units = "in", res = 1200)
print(plot)
while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()
```

### 1.02 TE composition
```{r, table1.02.01, echo=FALSE}
# TEGSm0_10000k
total_loci1 <- sum(data.sum1$count)
total_bp1 <- sum(data.sum1$bp)
total_fam1 <- sum(data.sum1$family_count)
data_sum1 <- data.sum1
data_sum1$total_loci <- rep(total_loci1, nrow(data_sum1))
data_sum1$total_bp <- rep(total_bp1, nrow(data_sum1))
data_sum1 <- data_sum1 %>% 
  mutate(loci_percentage = round(100*(count/total_loci), 2), bp_percentage = round(100*(bp/total_bp), 2), family_percentage = round(100*(family_count/total_fam1), 2)) %>%
  rename(TE_superfamily = TE, loci = count) %>%
  select(-total_loci, -total_bp)
total_row1 <- data.frame(TE_superfamily = "Total", loci = total_loci1, bp = total_bp1, family_count = total_fam1, loci_percentage = 100, bp_percentage = 100, family_percentage = 100)
data_sum1 <- rbind(data_sum1, total_row1)
data_sum1 <- data_sum1[order(data_sum1$TE_superfamily), ]
kable(data_sum1, format="markdown")
```

```{r, table1.02.02, echo=FALSE}
# denovoTEeval
total_loci2 <- sum(data.sum2$count)
total_bp2 <- sum(data.sum2$bp)
total_fam2 <- sum(data.sum2$family_count)
data_sum2 <- data.sum2
data_sum2$total_loci <- rep(total_loci2, nrow(data_sum2))
data_sum2$total_bp <- rep(total_bp2, nrow(data_sum2))
data_sum2 <- data_sum2 %>% 
  mutate(loci_percentage = round(100*(count/total_loci), 2), bp_percentage = round(100*(bp/total_bp), 2), family_percentage = round(100*(family_count/total_fam2), 2)) %>%
  rename(TE_superfamily = TE, loci = count) %>%
  select(-total_loci, -total_bp)
total_row2 <- data.frame(TE_superfamily = "Total", loci = total_loci2, bp = total_bp2, family_count = total_fam1, loci_percentage = 100, bp_percentage = 100, family_percentage = 100)
data_sum2 <- rbind(data_sum2, total_row2)
data_sum2 <- data_sum2[order(data_sum2$TE_superfamily), ]
kable(data_sum2, format="markdown")
```

#### Mean ± SD across 5 replicates (superfamilies pooled)

Bin mean/SD are extracted directly from the built histograms above via `ggplot_build()`
(`summarise_bins_from_histogram()`), rather than recomputed independently with `cut()` -
this guarantees the line graph and the histogram always agree on bin position/width/side.

```{r, fig1.04.meansd.stats, echo=FALSE}

                  bin_summary_dnvte_div$mean_count + bin_summary_dnvte_div$sd_count)) * 1.1
```

```{r, fig1.05.sup.stats, echo=FALSE}
# ymax derived from the data (per-replicate, per-bin stacked total can be much higher

    mutate(.bin = cut(itg, breaks = bin_breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, right = FALSE)) |>
    count(rep, .bin) |> pull(n)
)
ymax_sup <- ceiling(max_bin_count * 1.05 / 100) * 100
```

Fragment setting in denovoTE-eval:
```text
def fragment (seq):
    frag_size = 100
    len_seq =len(seq)
    if len_seq < 500:
        frag_size = random.randint(70,90)
    else:
        frag_size = random.randint(40,90)
    cut_length = int(len_seq*((100 - frag_size)/100.0))
    return seq[cut_length:], frag_size, cut_length
```

```{r, save_fig1.05.sup.dnvte, echo=FALSE}
print(plot)
while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()
```

### 2.01a t-test on simulated TE bases (n = 5 replicates)
Compares total simulated TE bases (`tesize`) between simulators. dnvTEe vs TEGS is a
two-sample Welch t-test (5 replicates each). Garlic/m2/m2+m0 vs Ori are one-sample
t-tests against Ori's single fixed value, since the original genome is not replicated.

```{r, ttest_tebases, echo=FALSE}
# x: replicate values being tested; y: replicate values of the second simulator (two-sample);
# mu: fixed reference value to test x's mean against (one-sample, used for comparisons vs Ori)
tidy_ttest <- function(comparison, x, y = NULL, mu = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(y)) {
    test <- t.test(x, y)
    mean1 <- mean(x); mean2 <- mean(y); ref_value <- NA_real_
    n1 <- length(x); n2 <- length(y)
    mean_diff <- mean1 - mean2
  } else {
    test <- t.test(x, mu = mu)
    mean1 <- mean(x); mean2 <- NA_real_; ref_value <- mu
    n1 <- length(x); n2 <- NA_integer_
    mean_diff <- mean1 - mu
  }
  data.frame(
    comparison = comparison,
    test_type = if (is.null(y)) "one-sample t-test (vs fixed Ori value)" else "two-sample t-test (Welch)",
    n1 = n1, n2 = n2,
    mean1_bases = mean1, mean2_bases = mean2, reference_bases = ref_value,
    mean_diff_bases = mean_diff,
    t_statistic = unname(test$statistic),
    df = unname(test$parameter),
    p_value = test$p.value,
    conf_low = test$conf.int[1], conf_high = test$conf.int[2],
    alternative = test$alternative,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

ttest_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidy_ttest("dnvTEe vs TEGS", x = dnvte_c1_stat$tesize, y = tegs_c1_stat$tesize),
  tidy_ttest("GARLIC vs Ori",  x = garlic_c2_stat$tesize, mu = ori_stat$tesize),
  tidy_ttest("m2 vs Ori",      x = m2_c2_stat$tesize,     mu = ori_stat$tesize),
  tidy_ttest("m2+m0 vs Ori",   x = m0_c2_stat$tesize,      mu = ori_stat$tesize),
  tidy_ttest("GARLIC vs m2",   x = garlic_c2_stat$tesize, y = m2_c2_stat$tesize),
  tidy_ttest("GARLIC vs m2+m0",  x = garlic_c2_stat$tesize, y = m0_c2_stat$tesize),
  tidy_ttest("m2 vs m2+m0",  x = m2_c2_stat$tesize, y = m0_c2_stat$tesize)
)

write.table(ttest_results, file = file.path(OUT, "tebases_ttest_results.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(ttest_results, digits = 4)
```

### 2.03a Jensen-Shannon divergence: TE composition by superfamily (per replicate)
Categorical distribution of TE bases and TE loci counts across superfamilies (as in
panels 1.02/1.03/2.02/2.03), compared per replicate for both metrics. dnvTEe vs TEGS
uses matched replicate pairs (rep i's dnvTEe run reuses rep i's TEGS composition
table). Garlic/m2/m2+m0 vs Ori compares each replicate to Ori's single fixed
distribution (the real chr1 is not replicated). Superfamily categories present in only
one side of a comparison are zero-filled, not dropped, so JSD is always computed over
the full union of categories.

```{r, jsd_superfamily, echo=FALSE}
source(file.path(WRK, "script/functions.R"))

# Jensen-Shannon divergence (log base 2, bounded [0,1] bit) between two superfamily
# composition vectors already aligned over the same set of category names.
jsd_divergence <- function(p, q) {
  p <- p / sum(p)
  q <- q / sum(q)
  m <- (p + q) / 2
  kl <- function(a, b) sum(ifelse(a > 0, a * log2(a / b), 0))
  0.5 * kl(p, m) + 0.5 * kl(q, m)
}

# list_a/list_b: lists of gff data.frames. If list_b has length 1 (e.g. Ori), that
# single reference is compared against every replicate in list_a; otherwise list_a
# and list_b are matched by replicate index (paired comparison). metric is "bp" or
# "count" (a column of te_by_superfamily_sim_genome()'s output).
jsd_between_reps <- function(list_a, list_b, comparison_label, metric = "bp") {
  n <- length(list_a)
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    gff_a <- list_a[[i]]
    gff_b <- if (length(list_b) == 1) list_b[[1]] else list_b[[i]]
    s_a <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(gff_a)
    s_b <- te_by_superfamily_sim_genome(gff_b)
    levels <- union(s_a$TE, s_b$TE)
    va <- setNames(rep(0, length(levels)), levels); va[s_a$TE] <- s_a[[metric]]
    vb <- setNames(rep(0, length(levels)), levels); vb[s_b$TE] <- s_b[[metric]]
    data.frame(comparison = comparison_label, rep = i, metric = metric, jsd = jsd_divergence(va, vb))
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(rows)
}

jsd_superfamily_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("bp", "count"), function(m){
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    jsd_between_reps(lapply(dnvte_c1_list, function(x) x$tegff), lapply(tegs_c1_list, function(x) x$tegff), "dnvTEe vs TEGS", metric = m),
    jsd_between_reps(lapply(garlic_c2_list, function(x) x$tegff), list(tegff0), "GARLIC vs Ori", metric = m),
    jsd_between_reps(lapply(m2_c2_list, function(x) x$tegff), list(tegff0), "m2 vs Ori", metric = m),
    jsd_between_reps(lapply(m0_c2_list, function(x) x$tegff), list(tegff0), "m2+m0 vs Ori", metric = m)
  )
}))
```

### 2.03b Superfamily-composition JSD: mean ± SD and significance testing
Mean ± SD summarised per comparison and metric. Significance testing follows the
replicate design of each comparison: dnvTEe vs TEGS is matched-pair by construction, so
its 5 JSD values (one per matched rep pair) are tested with a one-sample t-test against
mu = 0 (is the divergence between the two tools significantly non-zero, despite
matched input tables?). Garlic, m2, and m2+m0 replicates were each generated
independently of one another (no shared seed or composition table linking, say,
Garlic rep 3 to m2 rep 3), so their JSD-to-Ori values are compared pairwise with
unpaired (two-sample Welch) t-tests instead, to test which tool sits significantly
closer to Ori.

```{r, jsd_superfamily_meansd_ttest, echo=FALSE}
jsd_superfamily_summary <- jsd_superfamily_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(comparison, metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean_jsd = mean(jsd), sd_jsd = sd(jsd), .groups = "drop")

write.table(jsd_superfamily_summary, file = file.path(OUT, "jsd_superfamily_meansd.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(jsd_superfamily_summary, digits = 4)

# Generic one-sample (vs mu) or two-sample (unpaired) t-test summary row, reused for
# other distance/divergence metrics (Wasserstein, k-mer JSD) later in this notebook.
tidy_ttest_dist <- function(comparison, x, y = NULL, mu = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(y)) {
    test <- t.test(x, y)
    mean1 <- mean(x); mean2 <- mean(y); ref_value <- NA_real_
    n1 <- length(x); n2 <- length(y)
    mean_diff <- mean1 - mean2
  } else {
    test <- t.test(x, mu = mu)
    mean1 <- mean(x); mean2 <- NA_real_; ref_value <- mu
    n1 <- length(x); n2 <- NA_integer_
    mean_diff <- mean1 - mu
  }
  data.frame(
    comparison = comparison,
    test_type = if (is.null(y)) "one-sample t-test (vs mu)" else "two-sample t-test (Welch, unpaired)",
    n1 = n1, n2 = n2,
    mean1 = mean1, mean2 = mean2, reference = ref_value,
    mean_diff = mean_diff,
    t_statistic = unname(test$statistic),
    df = unname(test$parameter),
    p_value = test$p.value,
    conf_low = test$conf.int[1], conf_high = test$conf.int[2],
    alternative = test$alternative,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

get_jsd_vec <- function(cmp, m) jsd_superfamily_results |> dplyr::filter(comparison == cmp, metric == m) |> dplyr::pull(jsd)

# group1/group2 record which comparison(s) each row's x/y vectors came from (group2 is
# NA for the one-sample dnvTEe-vs-TEGS row); kept as explicit columns, rather than only
# embedded in the free-text `comparison` label, so downstream code (e.g. plotting) can
# join/filter on them directly instead of parsing the label string.
jsd_superfamily_ttests <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("bp", "count"), function(m){
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("dnvTEe vs TEGS (superfamily JSD, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_vec("dnvTEe vs TEGS", m), mu = 0) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "dnvTEe vs TEGS", group2 = NA_character_),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("GARLIC vs m2 (distance-to-Ori superfamily JSD, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_vec("GARLIC vs Ori", m), y = get_jsd_vec("m2 vs Ori", m)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "GARLIC vs Ori", group2 = "m2 vs Ori"),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("GARLIC vs m2+m0 (distance-to-Ori superfamily JSD, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_vec("GARLIC vs Ori", m), y = get_jsd_vec("m2+m0 vs Ori", m)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "GARLIC vs Ori", group2 = "m2+m0 vs Ori"),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("m2 vs m2+m0 (distance-to-Ori superfamily JSD, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_vec("m2 vs Ori", m), y = get_jsd_vec("m2+m0 vs Ori", m)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "m2 vs Ori", group2 = "m2+m0 vs Ori")
  )
}))

write.table(jsd_superfamily_ttests, file = file.path(OUT, "jsd_superfamily_ttest.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(jsd_superfamily_ttests, digits = 4)
```

Files saved as: jsd_superfamily_meansd.tsv, jsd_superfamily_ttest.tsv

### 2.03c Superfamily-composition JSD: bar plots (mean ± SD, asterisk if p < 0.001)
```{r, plot_jsd_superfamily_setup, echo=FALSE}
sig_asterisk <- function(p, cutoff = 0.001) ifelse(p < cutoff, "*", "ns")
```

#### Plot 1: dnvTEe vs TEGS (one-sample test per metric, asterisk above each bar)
```{r, plot_jsd_dnvte_tegs, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 3.4, fig.asp = 0.9}
plotwidth <- 3.4
plotheight <- 3.06
options(repr.plot.width=plotwidth, repr.plot.height=plotheight)

plot1_df <- jsd_superfamily_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(comparison == "dnvTEe vs TEGS") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    jsd_superfamily_ttests |> dplyr::filter(group1 == "dnvTEe vs TEGS", is.na(group2)) |>
      dplyr::select(metric, p_value),
    by = "metric"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric_label = factor(dplyr::recode(metric, bp = "TE bp", count = "TE loci count"),
                           levels = c("TE loci count", "TE bp")),
    sig_label = sig_asterisk(p_value)
  )

plot <- ggplot(plot1_df, aes(x = metric_label, y = mean_jsd, fill = metric_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_jsd - sd_jsd, ymax = mean_jsd + sd_jsd), width = 0.12) +
  geom_text(aes(y = mean_jsd + sd_jsd, label = sig_label), vjust = -0.6, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Jensen-Shannon divergence\n(superfamily composition)",
       title = "dnvTEe vs TEGS\n(mean ± SD, n=5;\none-sample t-test vs 0)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        title = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.3)))
plot
```


#### Plots 2 & 3: GARLIC/m2/m2+m0 vs Ori (pairwise unpaired tests, asterisk on brackets)
```{r, plot_jsd_ori_fn, echo=FALSE}
# Shared by the TE-loci-count and TE-bp versions below: bars = mean +/- SD per
# simulator's JSD-to-Ori values; brackets = the 3 pairwise unpaired t-tests among
# GARLIC/m2/m2+m0, staggered so the bracket spanning the two outer bars sits highest.
plot_jsd_ori_bars <- function(metric_val, ylab_text, title_text) {
  bars <- jsd_superfamily_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(comparison %in% c("GARLIC vs Ori", "m2 vs Ori", "m2+m0 vs Ori"), metric == metric_val) |>
    dplyr::mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = c("GARLIC vs Ori", "m2 vs Ori", "m2+m0 vs Ori")))

  top <- max(bars$mean_jsd + bars$sd_jsd)
  step <- top * 0.15

  stats <- jsd_superfamily_ttests |>
    dplyr::filter(metric == metric_val, !is.na(group2)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      group1 = factor(group1, levels = levels(bars$comparison)),
      group2 = factor(group2, levels = levels(bars$comparison)),
      p.signif = sig_asterisk(p_value),
      y.position = ifelse(group1 == "GARLIC vs Ori" & group2 == "m2+m0 vs Ori", top + 2 * step, top + step)
    )

  ggplot(bars, aes(x = comparison, y = mean_jsd, fill = comparison)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_jsd - sd_jsd, ymax = mean_jsd + sd_jsd), width = 0.12) +
    ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(stats, label = "p.signif", xmin = "group1", xmax = "group2",
                                y.position = "y.position", tip.length = 0.05, label.size = 5) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab_text, title = title_text) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          title = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4), angle = 30, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
          axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.3)))
}
```

#### Mean ± SD across replicates (superfamilies pooled; Ori not replicated)

Bin mean/SD are extracted via `ggplot_build()` from per-replicate histograms built
purely for that purpose (not displayed) - same approach as section 1, so the line
graph's bins always match what a histogram of the same data would show. Ori has only
one genome, so its line has no ribbon (SD is undefined for n=1).

```{r, fig2.04.meansd.build, echo=FALSE}
source(file.path(WRK, "script/functions.R"))
ymax_ph <- 1e6  # placeholder for the (unused/undisplayed) histogram's y-axis; never affects the extracted bin counts
hist_ori_div    <- plot_sim_divergence_by_loci_reps(breakdown0_allreps |> filter(div >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "Ori")
hist_garlic_div <- plot_sim_divergence_by_loci_reps(breakdown5_allreps |> filter(div >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "Garlic")
hist_m2_div     <- plot_sim_divergence_by_loci_reps(breakdown3_allreps |> filter(div >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "m2")
hist_m0_div     <- plot_sim_divergence_by_loci_reps(breakdown4_allreps |> filter(div >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "m2+m0")

bin_summary_ori_div    <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_ori_div)
bin_summary_garlic_div <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_garlic_div)
bin_summary_m2_div     <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_m2_div)
bin_summary_m0_div     <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_m0_div)

ymax_c2_div <- max(c(bin_summary_ori_div$mean_count,
                     bin_summary_garlic_div$mean_count + bin_summary_garlic_div$sd_count,
                     bin_summary_m2_div$mean_count + bin_summary_m2_div$sd_count,
                     bin_summary_m0_div$mean_count + bin_summary_m0_div$sd_count), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
```

#### Mean ± SD across replicates (superfamilies pooled; Ori not replicated)

```{r, fig2.05.meansd.build, echo=FALSE}
source(file.path(WRK, "script/functions.R"))
ymax_ph <- 1e6  # placeholder for the (unused/undisplayed) histogram's y-axis; never affects the extracted bin counts
hist_ori_itg    <- plot_sim_integrity_by_loci_reps(breakdown0_allreps |> filter(itg >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "Ori")
hist_garlic_itg <- plot_sim_integrity_by_loci_reps(breakdown5_allreps |> filter(itg >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "Garlic")
hist_m2_itg     <- plot_sim_integrity_by_loci_reps(breakdown3_allreps |> filter(itg >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "m2")
hist_m0_itg     <- plot_sim_integrity_by_loci_reps(breakdown4_allreps |> filter(itg >= 0), ymax_ph, ymax_ph/5, "m2+m0")

bin_summary_ori_itg    <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_ori_itg)
bin_summary_garlic_itg <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_garlic_itg)
bin_summary_m2_itg     <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_m2_itg)
bin_summary_m0_itg     <- summarise_bins_from_histogram(hist_m0_itg)

                     bin_summary_garlic_itg$mean_count + bin_summary_garlic_itg$sd_count,

                     bin_summary_m0_itg$mean_count + bin_summary_m0_itg$sd_count), na.rm = TRUE) * 1.1
```

### 2.05a Wasserstein distance: TE loci divergence and integrity (per replicate)
1D (earth-mover's) Wasserstein distance between raw per-locus divergence (`div`) and
integrity (`itg`) values (superfamilies pooled, as in Fig. 2's mean ± SD panels above),
computed per replicate using the same `breakdown*_allreps` tables built earlier in this
notebook. Unlike JSD (Point 1), Wasserstein operates directly on the continuous raw
values rather than a binned/categorical distribution, so no bin-width choice is
involved. dnvTEe vs TEGS is paired by replicate index (rep i's dnvTEe run reuses rep
i's TEGS composition table); Garlic/m2/m2+m0 vs Ori compares each replicate against
Ori's single fixed distribution (`breakdown0_allreps`, not replicated).

```{r, wasserstein_div_itg, echo=FALSE}
# Exact 1D Wasserstein (earth-mover's) distance between two empirical samples of
# possibly different size, via the area between their empirical CDFs - equivalent to
# scipy.stats.wasserstein_distance.
wasserstein1d <- function(u, v) {
  u <- sort(as.numeric(u)); v <- sort(as.numeric(v))
  all_values <- sort(c(u, v))
  n <- length(all_values)
  deltas <- diff(all_values)
  bp <- all_values[-n]
  u_cdf <- findInterval(bp, u) / length(u)
  v_cdf <- findInterval(bp, v) / length(v)
  sum(abs(u_cdf - v_cdf) * deltas)
}

# df_a/df_b: breakdown*_allreps tables (columns rep, div, itg, ...). If single_ref =
# TRUE, df_b is used as one fixed reference distribution (e.g. Ori) for every
# replicate in df_a; otherwise df_a and df_b are matched by replicate index (paired
# comparison, e.g. dnvTEe vs TEGS).
wasserstein_between_reps <- function(df_a, df_b, comparison_label, value_col, single_ref = FALSE) {
  reps <- sort(unique(df_a$rep))
  rows <- lapply(reps, function(i) {
    x <- df_a |> dplyr::filter(rep == i, .data[[value_col]] >= 0) |> dplyr::pull(.data[[value_col]])
    if (single_ref) {
      y <- df_b |> dplyr::filter(.data[[value_col]] >= 0) |> dplyr::pull(.data[[value_col]])
    } else {
      y <- df_b |> dplyr::filter(rep == i, .data[[value_col]] >= 0) |> dplyr::pull(.data[[value_col]])
    }
    data.frame(comparison = comparison_label, rep = i, metric = value_col,
               wasserstein = wasserstein1d(x, y))
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(rows)
}

wasserstein_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("div", "itg"), function(v){
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    wasserstein_between_reps(breakdown2_allreps, breakdown1_allreps, "dnvTEe vs TEGS", v, single_ref = FALSE),
    wasserstein_between_reps(breakdown5_allreps, breakdown0_allreps, "GARLIC vs Ori",  v, single_ref = TRUE),
    wasserstein_between_reps(breakdown3_allreps, breakdown0_allreps, "m2 vs Ori",      v, single_ref = TRUE),
    wasserstein_between_reps(breakdown4_allreps, breakdown0_allreps, "m2+m0 vs Ori",   v, single_ref = TRUE)
  )
}))

write.table(wasserstein_results, file = file.path(OUT, "wasserstein_divergence_integrity_per_replicate.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(wasserstein_results, digits = 4)
```

File saved as: wasserstein_divergence_integrity_per_replicate.tsv (columns: comparison,
rep, metric ["div"/"itg"], wasserstein)

### 2.05b Wasserstein distance: mean ± SD and significance testing
Same design as the superfamily-JSD testing in 2.03b, applied to the Wasserstein
distances: dnvTEe vs TEGS is matched-pair by construction, so its 5 distance values are
tested with a one-sample t-test against mu = 0. Garlic/m2/m2+m0 replicates were each
generated independently of one another, so their distance-to-Ori values are compared
pairwise with unpaired (two-sample Welch) t-tests. Reuses `tidy_ttest_dist()` defined
in section 2.03b.

```{r, wasserstein_meansd_ttest, echo=FALSE}
wasserstein_summary <- wasserstein_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(comparison, metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean_wasserstein = mean(wasserstein), sd_wasserstein = sd(wasserstein), .groups = "drop")

write.table(wasserstein_summary, file = file.path(OUT, "wasserstein_meansd.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(wasserstein_summary, digits = 4)

get_wasserstein_vec <- function(cmp, m) wasserstein_results |> dplyr::filter(comparison == cmp, metric == m) |> dplyr::pull(wasserstein)

wasserstein_ttests <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("div", "itg"), function(m){
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("dnvTEe vs TEGS (Wasserstein, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_wasserstein_vec("dnvTEe vs TEGS", m), mu = 0) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "dnvTEe vs TEGS", group2 = NA_character_),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("GARLIC vs m2 (distance-to-Ori Wasserstein, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_wasserstein_vec("GARLIC vs Ori", m), y = get_wasserstein_vec("m2 vs Ori", m)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "GARLIC vs Ori", group2 = "m2 vs Ori"),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("GARLIC vs m2+m0 (distance-to-Ori Wasserstein, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_wasserstein_vec("GARLIC vs Ori", m), y = get_wasserstein_vec("m2+m0 vs Ori", m)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "GARLIC vs Ori", group2 = "m2+m0 vs Ori"),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("m2 vs m2+m0 (distance-to-Ori Wasserstein, ", m, ")"),
                     x = get_wasserstein_vec("m2 vs Ori", m), y = get_wasserstein_vec("m2+m0 vs Ori", m)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(metric = m, group1 = "m2 vs Ori", group2 = "m2+m0 vs Ori")
  )
}))

write.table(wasserstein_ttests, file = file.path(OUT, "wasserstein_ttest.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(wasserstein_ttests, digits = 4)
```

Files saved as: wasserstein_meansd.tsv, wasserstein_ttest.tsv

#### Plots 2 & 3: GARLIC/m2/m2+m0 vs Ori (pairwise unpaired tests, asterisk on brackets)
```{r, plot_wasserstein_ori_fn, echo=FALSE}
# Shared by the divergence and integrity versions below: bars = mean +/- SD per
# simulator's Wasserstein-distance-to-Ori values; brackets = the 3 pairwise unpaired
# t-tests among GARLIC/m2/m2+m0, staggered so the bracket spanning the two outer bars
# sits highest.
plot_wasserstein_ori_bars <- function(metric_val, ylab_text, title_text) {
  bars <- wasserstein_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(comparison %in% c("GARLIC vs Ori", "m2 vs Ori", "m2+m0 vs Ori"), metric == metric_val) |>
    dplyr::mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = c("GARLIC vs Ori", "m2 vs Ori", "m2+m0 vs Ori")))

  top <- max(bars$mean_wasserstein + bars$sd_wasserstein)
  step <- top * 0.15

  stats <- wasserstein_ttests |>
    dplyr::filter(metric == metric_val, !is.na(group2)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      group1 = factor(group1, levels = levels(bars$comparison)),
      group2 = factor(group2, levels = levels(bars$comparison)),
      p.signif = sig_asterisk(p_value),
      y.position = ifelse(group1 == "GARLIC vs Ori" & group2 == "m2+m0 vs Ori", top + 2 * step, top + step)
    )

  ggplot(bars, aes(x = comparison, y = mean_wasserstein, fill = comparison)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_wasserstein - sd_wasserstein, ymax = mean_wasserstein + sd_wasserstein), width = 0.12) +
    ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(stats, label = "p.signif", xmin = "group1", xmax = "group2",
                                y.position = "y.position", tip.length = 0.05, label.size = 5) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab_text, title = title_text) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          title = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4), angle = 30, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
          axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.3)))
}
```

### 2.06a Jensen-Shannon divergence: k-mer spectrum (per replicate)
Canonical 6-mer count spectra (as in panel 2.06/Fig. 2G), compared per replicate for
each of the three sequence categories (whole genome, non-TE, TE-only). Unlike the
JSD/Wasserstein sections above, this only covers Comparison 2 (GARLIC/m2/m2+m0 vs Ori)
- `item30_te_sim_eval_raw.sh` was never run for dnvTEe/TEGS (Comparison 1), so no
k-mer data exists for that comparison. The k-mer vocabulary (2080 canonical 6-mers) is
fixed and identical across all replicates/tools (same Python enumeration), so unlike
the superfamily JSD, no union/zero-fill is needed - counts are matched by the `kmer`
column via a join, as a safety check against any row-order difference between files.
Reuses `jsd_divergence()` defined in section 2.03a.

```{r, jsd_kmer, echo=FALSE}
jsd_between_reps_kmer <- function(rep_paths, ref_path, comparison_label, category) {
  ref_df <- read.table(ref_path, header = TRUE, sep = ",", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(rep_paths), function(i) {
    df_a <- read.table(rep_paths[i], header = TRUE, sep = ",", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    merged <- merge(df_a[, c("kmer", category)], ref_df[, c("kmer", category)],
                     by = "kmer", suffixes = c("_a", "_ref"))
    data.frame(comparison = comparison_label, rep = i, category = category,
               jsd = jsd_divergence(merged[[paste0(category, "_a")]], merged[[paste0(category, "_ref")]]))
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(rows)
}

m2_kmer_paths     <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/TE_sim_eval/tair10_ch1_m2_%d/kmer/kmer_counts_k6.csv', reps))
m0_kmer_paths     <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/TE_sim_eval/tair10_ch1_m0_%d/kmer/kmer_counts_k6.csv', reps))
garlic_kmer_paths <- file.path(WRK, sprintf('output/TE_sim_eval/Garlic_rep%d/kmer/kmer_counts_k6.csv', reps))
ori_kmer_path     <- file.path(WRK, 'output/TE_sim_eval/original/kmer/kmer_counts_k6.csv')

jsd_kmer_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("genome", "nonTE", "TEonly"), function(cat){
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    jsd_between_reps_kmer(garlic_kmer_paths, ori_kmer_path, "GARLIC vs Ori", cat),
    jsd_between_reps_kmer(m2_kmer_paths,     ori_kmer_path, "m2 vs Ori",     cat),
    jsd_between_reps_kmer(m0_kmer_paths,     ori_kmer_path, "m2+m0 vs Ori",  cat)
  )
}))

write.table(jsd_kmer_results, file = file.path(OUT, "jsd_kmer_spectrum_per_replicate.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(jsd_kmer_results, digits = 4)
```

["genome"/"nonTE"/"TEonly"], jsd)

### 2.06b k-mer spectrum JSD: mean ± SD and significance testing
Only the three GARLIC/m2/m2+m0-vs-Ori groups exist here (no dnvTEe/TEGS k-mer data, as
noted in 2.06a), so there is no one-sample paired-difference test to run - all three
comparisons are independent replicate sets, tested pairwise with unpaired (two-sample
Welch) t-tests, same as the Garlic/m2/m2+m0 rows in 2.03b/2.05b. Reuses
`tidy_ttest_dist()` from section 2.03b.

```{r, jsd_kmer_meansd_ttest, echo=FALSE}
jsd_kmer_summary <- jsd_kmer_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(comparison, category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), mean_jsd = mean(jsd), sd_jsd = sd(jsd), .groups = "drop")

write.table(jsd_kmer_summary, file = file.path(OUT, "jsd_kmer_meansd.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(jsd_kmer_summary, digits = 4)

get_jsd_kmer_vec <- function(cmp, cat) jsd_kmer_results |> dplyr::filter(comparison == cmp, category == cat) |> dplyr::pull(jsd)

jsd_kmer_ttests <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("genome", "nonTE", "TEonly"), function(cat){
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("GARLIC vs m2 (k-mer JSD, ", cat, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_kmer_vec("GARLIC vs Ori", cat), y = get_jsd_kmer_vec("m2 vs Ori", cat)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(category = cat, group1 = "GARLIC vs Ori", group2 = "m2 vs Ori"),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("GARLIC vs m2+m0 (k-mer JSD, ", cat, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_kmer_vec("GARLIC vs Ori", cat), y = get_jsd_kmer_vec("m2+m0 vs Ori", cat)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(category = cat, group1 = "GARLIC vs Ori", group2 = "m2+m0 vs Ori"),
    tidy_ttest_dist(paste0("m2 vs m2+m0 (k-mer JSD, ", cat, ")"),
                     x = get_jsd_kmer_vec("m2 vs Ori", cat), y = get_jsd_kmer_vec("m2+m0 vs Ori", cat)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(category = cat, group1 = "m2 vs Ori", group2 = "m2+m0 vs Ori")
  )
}))

write.table(jsd_kmer_ttests, file = file.path(OUT, "jsd_kmer_ttest.tsv"),
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(jsd_kmer_ttests, digits = 4)
```

Files saved as: jsd_kmer_meansd.tsv, jsd_kmer_ttest.tsv

### 2.06c k-mer spectrum JSD: bar plots (mean ± SD, asterisk if p < 0.001)
Same layout as 2.03c/2.05c, but only the 3-bar GARLIC/m2/m2+m0-vs-Ori style applies
here (no dnvTEe/TEGS k-mer data), so there's one plot per sequence category instead of
a separate one-sample plot. Reuses `sig_asterisk()` from 2.03c.

```{r, plot_jsd_kmer_ori_fn, echo=FALSE}
# Shared by the genome/nonTE/TEonly versions below: bars = mean +/- SD per simulator's
# k-mer-JSD-to-Ori values; brackets = the 3 pairwise unpaired t-tests among
# GARLIC/m2/m2+m0, staggered so the bracket spanning the two outer bars sits highest.
plot_jsd_kmer_ori_bars <- function(category_val, ylab_text, title_text) {
  bars <- jsd_kmer_summary |>
    dplyr::filter(comparison %in% c("GARLIC vs Ori", "m2 vs Ori", "m2+m0 vs Ori"), category == category_val) |>
    dplyr::mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = c("GARLIC vs Ori", "m2 vs Ori", "m2+m0 vs Ori")))

  top <- max(bars$mean_jsd + bars$sd_jsd)
  step <- top * 0.15

  stats <- jsd_kmer_ttests |>
    dplyr::filter(category == category_val) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      group1 = factor(group1, levels = levels(bars$comparison)),
      group2 = factor(group2, levels = levels(bars$comparison)),
      p.signif = sig_asterisk(p_value),
      y.position = ifelse(group1 == "GARLIC vs Ori" & group2 == "m2+m0 vs Ori", top + 2 * step, top + step)
    )

  ggplot(bars, aes(x = comparison, y = mean_jsd, fill = comparison)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_jsd - sd_jsd, ymax = mean_jsd + sd_jsd), width = 0.12) +
    ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(stats, label = "p.signif", xmin = "group1", xmax = "group2",
                                y.position = "y.position", tip.length = 0.05, label.size = 7) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab_text, title = title_text) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          title = element_text(size = 10),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4), angle = 30, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
          axis.title.x = element_text(size = rel(1.4)),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = rel(1.3)))
}
```

```{r, plot_jsd_kmer_ori_genome, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 4.2, fig.asp = 0.85}

                               "k-mer JSD to Ori: whole genome\n(mean ± SD, n=5; unpaired t-tests)")
plot
```

```{r, test_entropy_range, echo=FALSE}
entrdf_fil <- entrdf |> filter(simulator != "m0full") |> filter(entropy > 0)

# Kruskal-Wallis test
kruskal_res <- kruskal.test(entropy ~ simulator, data = entrdf_fil)
kruskal_res

# Pairwise post-hoc comparisons
pairwise_res <- pairwise.wilcox.test(entrdf_fil$entropy, entrdf_fil$simulator, p.adjust.method = "BH")
pairwise_res

# Pairwise post-hoc comparisons by category
entrdf_fil_genome <- entrdf_fil |> filter(Category == "genome")
pairwise_res_genome <- pairwise.wilcox.test(entrdf_fil_genome$entropy, entrdf_fil_genome$simulator, p.adjust.method = "BH")
pairwise_res_genome
entrdf_fil_nonTE <- entrdf_fil |> filter(Category == "nonTE")
pairwise_res_nonTE <- pairwise.wilcox.test(entrdf_fil_nonTE$entropy, entrdf_fil_nonTE$simulator, p.adjust.method = "BH")
pairwise_res_nonTE
entrdf_fil_TEonly <- entrdf_fil |> filter(Category == "TEonly")
pairwise_res_TEonly <- pairwise.wilcox.test(entrdf_fil_TEonly$entropy, entrdf_fil_TEonly$simulator, p.adjust.method = "BH")
pairwise_res_TEonly
```
